tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local replay of four crash windows around the prior six-field coordination record {generation_id, stable_effect_key, payload_hash, evidence-qualified acceptance_state, accepted_result reference/digest when known, authority_epoch}. The replay tests: (a) authority E1 is durably acquired while the effect record still contains E0, (b) the record CAS advances to E1 but retry has not started, (c) atomic apply_once(K1,H1) accepts but the accepted-result checkpoint is lost, and (d) the accepted-result checkpoint succeeds but the invocation dies before normal return. It tests abstract ordering/CAS requirements only; no concrete transport, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is modeled.

crash_windows.event: E1 is durably acquired but the effect record still says E0.
crash_windows.safe_recovery: Every effect attempt and every authority-sensitive record mutation must be rejected unless its fence token equals the currently active monotonic authority token. Therefore stale A0/E0 cannot remain executable merely because the effect record has not yet been rewritten. Record propagation from E0 to E1 may lag only if the active authority/fence check is independent and authoritative.
crash_windows.failure_control: If stale-claimant rejection consults only record_authority_epoch, the E1-acquired/E0-record window permits A0 to act and safety is not established.

crash_windows.event: A CAS updates record authority from E0 to E1, preserving G1/K1/H1 and unknown acceptance, then the invocation dies before retry.
crash_windows.safe_recovery: A successor reading E1 resumes the same G1/K1/H1 and keeps acceptance unknown; no new key is minted and no accepted/nonaccepted inference is made. The authority update CAS must be monotonic and must not rewrite generation, effect key, payload hash, or acceptance evidence as a side effect.

crash_windows.event: apply_once(K1,H1) atomically accepts R1 but the result-reference checkpoint is lost.
crash_windows.safe_recovery: The durable record remains unknown, so recovery retries the same K1/H1 under the current fence. The sink must return the already-bound R1 or equivalent definitive accepted evidence without applying the effect again. Only that returned durable evidence may advance acceptance_state to verified_accepted and attach the result reference/digest.
crash_windows.failure_control: Rotating to K2 can duplicate G1; changing unknown to not_accepted can duplicate; changing unknown to accepted without result/atomic evidence can falsely suppress an effect that may never have committed.

crash_windows.event: The record checkpoint durably stores verified_accepted plus R1 reference/digest and the invocation dies before normal return.
crash_windows.safe_recovery: The next invocation treats the accepted record as terminal for that logical effect generation and does not execute another side effect. Normal-return acknowledgement is not part of effect identity and must not trigger K1 rotation or replay-as-new-work.

minimum_ordering_and_cas_invariants: I1: Authority/fence epochs are monotonic; a lower epoch can never regain authority after a higher epoch becomes active.

I2: Every effect attempt and every authority-sensitive state mutation validates the currently active fence atomically enough that stale A0/E0 cannot act during the E1-acquired/E0-record propagation window; if no such primitive exists, crash window A remains unsafe.
I3: Claimant turnover changes authority epoch only. For the same logical generation, generation_id G1, effect_key K1 and payload_hash H1 are immutable across retries until acceptance is resolved.
I4: Record CAS compares an expected prior record version/epoch and preserves immutable generation/key/hash fields. A stale claimant cannot overwrite a newer epoch or move acceptance backward.

I5: acceptance_state is monotonic in evidence strength: unknown/pending may become verified_accepted only from durable atomic acceptance/result evidence; it may not be converted to accepted or not_accepted merely from attempt-start, timeout, acknowledgement loss, or invocation return status.
I6: apply_once is keyed by K1 and bound to H1. A repeated K1/H1 returns the same accepted result/evidence; K1/H2 is an explicit conflict; K2 for the same unresolved G1 is forbidden.
I7: Once verified_accepted plus result reference/digest is durably checkpointed, crash/restart and missing normal return cannot reopen the generation for another effect execution.

observations: The six-field record alone is insufficient to close crash window A if current authority is inferred only from that same lagging record. A distinct monotonic fence authority, or an equivalent atomic activation protocol, is required so a newly active E1 immediately invalidates E0 even before record propagation completes.

Crash windows B-D do not require a fresh effect identity. Safety depends on preserving G1/K1/H1, keeping unknown acceptance epistemically honest, and making verified acceptance monotonic once supported by durable atomic evidence.

Invocation completion is not an effect-commit signal. The durable effect record and sink idempotency evidence, not whether the Chat invocation returned normally, determine whether the logical effect may execute again.
CAS must protect both authority monotonicity and non-regression of acceptance evidence; otherwise a stale claimant can overwrite E1 or regress verified_accepted to unknown and reopen execution.
inference: Within this exact abstract replay, crash-safe claimant turnover requires two coupled but distinct mechanisms: monotonic fencing for who may act now, and stable idempotency identity for what logical effect is being retried. The minimum safety ordering is that E1 activation invalidates E0 before any E1 retry is permitted; thereafter the effect record may be CAS-updated to E1 while preserving G1/K1/H1 and unknown acceptance. Lost acknowledgements are recovered by same-key apply_once replay, and only durable atomic result evidence may close acceptance. These invariants are necessary for the modeled crashes but are not sufficient evidence for a concrete scheduled-Chat implementation because an allowed primitive providing current-fence validation, CAS durability, atomic apply-once and reconstruction under quota-zero/rate-limit interruption remains unverified.
unresolved_children: Verify a concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed mechanism whose authority operation provides monotonic current-fence validation across crash window A.
Verify a concrete allowed CAS/state surface that preserves G1/K1/H1 and prevents stale-epoch or acceptance-regression writes without hosted coordination.
Verify a concrete allowed atomic apply-once or equivalent sink dedup primitive that binds K1 to H1 and can return prior accepted evidence after acknowledgement loss.
Verify reconstruction and eventual-progress behavior under repository/API rate limiting with no finite quota, hosted compute, richer mode, protected authority, or manual user execution.
